messages:
incident-bot: Pager — Alarm: NAT-OutboundErrors (eu-west-3) exceeded threshold -> >5% for 5m. Severity: potential customer impact. Incident channel created. Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.ai/nat-outbound-errors :rotating_light:
sre-oncall-sarah: I'm on it. Looking at metrics now, will post findings. Any immediate customer reports?
miguel-support: Getting a spike of tickets: several customers reporting outbound webhook failures to payment provider, started ~10:12 UTC. Errors are 502/504 and connection resets.
elaine-netops: On VPC side seeing a flurry of ReplaceRouteTableAssociation events at 10:10 UTC. Some private subnets are now associated with rtb-locked (restrictive). NAT gateways still attached but routes to 0.0.0.0/0 point to blackhole in that table.
jay-platform: I ran a compliance rollout earlier and applied a TF change to lock egress for a subset of private subnets. I didn't expect it to touch associations but the apply went through at 10:10. I'm reviewing.
darren-infra: Confirmed in CloudTrail: ReplaceRouteTableAssociation by user jay-platform at 2026-03-15T10:10:34Z. Association rta-0a1b2c -> now uses rtb-locked. That route table has no nat route and NACL rules deny ephemeral ports. Likely root cause for outbound failures.
sre-oncall-sarah: OK mitigation plan: 1) re-associate affected subnets back to rtb-default 2) restore NACL egress for ephemeral ports 1024-65535 3) validate NAT metrics + payment gateway success 4) customer comms. Who can execute 1/2?
jay-platform: I'm on the rollout. I'll cancel the TF run and do manual re-assoc if needed. Cancelling now.
ops-rotation-bot: Reminder: on-call handover in 40m. Adding note to keep channel updated.
darren-infra: Running manual re-association now:
```bash
aws ec2 replace-route-table-association --association-id rta-0a1b2c3d --route-table-id rtb-0123456789abcdef0 --region eu-west-3
```
Response: Association replaced. Re-assoc to rtb-default succeeded.
incident-bot: Deploy bot: terraform run t-20270321 canceled by jay-platform.
jay-platform: I canceled the automated apply and performed the replace-route-table-association. Double-checking state and connectivity.
elaine-netops: NACL had rule 100: deny egress 0.0.0.0/0 tcp 1024-65535. Updating to allow, applying replace-network-acl-entry.
```bash
aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id nacl-0abc1234 --rule-number 100 --protocol tcp --port-range From=1024,To=65535 --egress --rule-action allow --region eu-west-3
```
elaine-netops: NACL updated.
sre-oncall-sarah: NAT metrics trending down: OutboundErrors dropped from ~12% to ~0.8% over 8m. ELB target health failing count decreasing. Can someone confirm payment provider now receiving traffic?
miguel-support: Payment provider logs show successful callbacks resuming at 10:20 UTC. Customer ops sent initial status update.
jay-platform: Quick note on root cause: TF snippet that caused the change used a for_each over var.private_subnets and associated aws_route_table.locked without a manual approval gate. Example that went wrong:
```hcl
resource "aws_route_table_association" "restrict" {
  for_each = var.private_subnets
  subnet_id = each.value
  route_table_id = aws_route_table.locked.id
}
```
Because of state drift in one subnet, the plan replaced an association unexpectedly.
sre-oncall-sarah: Impact summary: Sev2 -> partial outage for egress-dependent features in eu-west-3. ~18 customers experienced transient payment/webhook failures. Mitigation applied; monitoring in progress. Incident page: https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-20789
ops-rotation-bot: Handoff: @sre-oncall-sarah please assign postmortem owner and follow-ups.
sre-oncall-sarah: Assigning postmortem owners: jay-platform, darren-infra. I'll draft timeline and initial notes.
darren-infra: Proposed action items: 1) Prevent route_table_association changes in routine rollouts without approval gate. 2) Add pre-apply diffs for associations and NACLs in CI. 3) Add post-apply sanity checks verifying NAT egress and ephemeral port access.
elaine-netops: Also propose infra test that simulates egress to third-party endpoints and fails CI if blocked. Block adding NACL denies for ephemeral ranges for private subnets.
miguel-support: Customer comms: sent update at 10:35 UTC stating mitigation in progress and that services are restoring. No legal/PCI escalations yet.
sre-oncall-sarah: Monitoring status: NAT error rate stabilized ~0.2% over 20m, no new alert. Will close pager in 30m if stable.
incident-bot: Incident status changed to mitigated. Severity lowered to Sev3. Created follow-up ticket INF-20789-POSTMORTEM.
jay-platform: Sorry team. I will own the postmortem and implement the approval gate + CI diffs.
miguel-support: I've attached affected customer logs/IDs to the incident page for callbacks.
sre-oncall-sarah: Thanks everyone — closing this channel for active mitigation. Postmortem due by EOD, follow-ups within 48h. :white_check_mark:
